notes: Battle stages of the original's stage table at 0x2212ac, keyed by port names. model is the stage's converted glTF (tools/phantomcrash.py convert writes models/model/<name>.gltf from Media/model/<name>.bin).
sky_nodes are drawn around the camera and behind everything: the stage object list (0x2212ec) puts the sky mesh in view layer 1.

The training ground (stage 6, the tutorial battle of scene 42) is choco_mdl: resource 1564 texture/choco_tex binds its textures; its object slots 900-906 are meshes 0-6. Stage 7, choco_night, is the training ground at night: slots 907-916 are meshes 0-9, and meshes 4 and 5 are in view layer 1 (the sky).

scene_stage is the stage's number in the original's tables (0x2212ac): the battle takes its gates, doors, fixed cameras and supply routes from tables/battle_scenes.json under it. door_model is the effect model its gate doors' leaves are drawn from (meshes 4 and 5; resource 0x492 on stage 6, 0x498 on stage 7). Either one left out keeps the training file's battle.scenes values.

collision is the stage's converted collision (tools/phantomcrash.py convert-robots writes collision/<name>.json from the resource at 0x2212cc: walls pushed against as spheres, floor under the robots). Without it the battle falls back to the training file's box arena.

lighting and fog are the stage's first environment preset (the list at 0x2014c8; tools/phantomcrash.py convert-robots writes them all to tables/environment.json): the training ground uses Fix1. sun_direction is the stage's light vector (0x2015f8), the way the light travels. sun_colour is the light colour times its diffuse scale and ambient the colour times its ambient scale (0x044e9f). Fog is linear in distance from the eye; clear_colour is the fog colour. shadow_colour is what the robots' shadow volumes lay over the stage (the table at 0x2014e8 by stage: 0x70030303, 0x32030303 on stage 3). Colours are 0-1, as the original's 0-255 over 255.

screen is the frame's last pass before the cockpit (0x0b7900): tint_argb is the preset's four ints at +0x24 (A, R, G, B, packed into 0x25b490 by 0x0b20a0), multiplied into every pixel; depth_of_field is the battle blur (0x0b5fb0), on in every battle (0x046aa5). The blur mixes a twice-softened copy (four taps one texel out, of the 640x480 frame then of its half; blur_texels) in by saturate((depth byte - (focus * focus_scale + focus_base)) * ramp), the depth byte being the top byte of the original's depth under its battle projection (depth_near 0.1, depth_far 10000, 0x0b7cc0). focus is the table at 0x203820 (80 on every stage); the original lowers it by up to 10 from a field of the player's camera word (+0x9cc bits 20-29), not ported. Left out, focus_scale 0.0005, focus_base 0.95, ramp 32, blur_texels 1.
